learningObjective: Distinguish weight-only, W8A8, and W4A16 quantization schemes by their memory-traffic and kernel-support profiles.

canonicalClaims.claim: W4A16 targets bandwidth-bound decode by halving weight HBM traffic vs INT8, using dequant-in-register to keep compute in FP16 Tensor Cores; W8A8 targets compute-bound cases by using INT8 Tensor Cores whose peak TOPS exceed FP16 TFLOPS; W8A16 is a lightweight weight-only halving with no activation calibration burden.
conditions: The GPU has FP16 Tensor Cores (Ampere+).
Appropriate kernels are available (Marlin/ExLlama for W4A16; cuBLAS/CUTLASS INT8 for W8A8).
nonImplications: Does not imply W4A16 beats W8A8 for large-batch prefill; compute dominance flips the winner.
Does not imply weight-only quantization is accuracy-free; RTN/GPTQ/AWQ have different quality profiles.

misconceptions.claim: W4A16 requires INT4 Tensor Cores to work.
misconceptions.whyWrong: W4A16 kernels typically dequant INT4 to FP16 in registers and use FP16 Tensor Cores; INT4 Tensor Cores are not required.

misconceptions.claim: Any quantization scheme is always faster than FP16 because the model is smaller.
misconceptions.whyWrong: 'Smaller' does not imply 'faster'; kernel availability, activation calibration, and compute-vs-bandwidth ratio determine wall-clock outcome.

misconceptions.claim: W8A8 requires no activation calibration; the runtime quantizes activations on-the-fly at no cost.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamic quantization of activations adds per-request scale computation; static quantization requires an offline calibration pass with representative data.

misconceptions.claim: For batch-1 decode, W8A8 is faster than W4A16 because INT8 Tensor Cores have higher TOPS.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Batch-1 decode is bandwidth-bound on weights; INT8 Tensor Core peak throughput cannot be reached, so W4A16's bandwidth advantage wins.

implementationFacts: Marlin (INT4 W4A16 kernel) achieves near-FP16-bandwidth-limit throughput on Ampere.
cuBLAS Lt supports INT8 GEMM with per-channel weight scales and per-tensor activation scales.
performanceScenarios: LLaMA-70B decode batch=1: W4A16 (AWQ) ~2× faster than FP16, while W8A8 (SmoothQuant) is closer to 1.2× at that batch.
